name: sqlmap
one_line: automatic SQL injection and database takeover tool
plain: `sqlmap` tests a web request for SQL injection and, when it finds a hole, can list databases, tables and columns and dump the data. It automates what you would otherwise do by hand with quotes and UNION SELECT.

Give it a URL with a parameter (or a saved request) and it tries many injection techniques, learns the database type and shows what it can read. It only works on targets where you have permission, such as a CTF or your own lab.
when: Check whether a parameter is injectable.
List databases, tables and columns of a vulnerable lab app.
Dump a table that holds the flag.
Reuse a request captured in Burp.

examples.title: Test a URL parameter
examples.explain: -u names the target; the parameter to test is the one in the query string. --batch accepts the defaults so no questions are asked.

examples.title: List the databases
examples.explain: --dbs asks the injected query for the names of the databases.

examples.title: List tables, then dump one
examples.explain: -D picks a database, -T a table. --dump downloads every row. Do it in two steps so you only take what you need.

examples.title: Use a saved request
examples.explain: -r reads a raw HTTP request you saved from Burp, including cookies and POST body.

examples.title: A POST form
examples.explain: --data gives the POST body and -p chooses the field to test.

examples.title: Raise the level of testing
examples.explain: --level adds more places to test (cookies, headers); --risk adds heavier payloads. Higher is slower and noisier.

examples.title: Read a file
examples.explain: Asks the database to read a file from the server, if the database user has the right. Lab targets only.

mistakes: Running --dump-all on a big database: slow and loud. Take one table.
Letting --batch make choices you did not review.
Forgetting cookies: the page then redirects to login and everything looks safe.
Using it on systems you are not authorised to test.
try: Capture a request in Burp, save it and run sqlmap -r on a lab app.
List databases, then tables, then dump only the users table.
Crack any password hash you get with john.
see_also: burpsuite, curl(1), john(8), hashcat(1), and the OWASP SQL injection pages.
captured_with: Examples are written to explain a technique; they are not captured output.
